# Vancouver Daily News
> **After eighteen months, David Eby ruled out Metro Vancouver's vehicle levy.**

**What You Need to Know:** NDP Leader David Eby has ruled out a Metro Vancouver vehicle levy that TransLink has discussed for 18 months as fuel-tax revenue declines. Police ticket counts, extortion charges and a West Vancouver crash trial are also in today's brief, with a new provincial sales tax on textiles and tailoring.

### Top Stories
**Eby rules out a Metro Vancouver vehicle levy: CBC British Columbia**
NDP Leader David Eby has ruled out a vehicle levy for Metro Vancouver. TransLink has talked about that levy for the last 18 months as a way to build a more sustainable funding model while revenue from fuel taxes continues to decline. CBC reports that a nearly $14-billion deficit made the levy politically unviable from the NDP leader's perspective. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/david-eby-bc-ndp-vehicle-levy-transit-metro-vancouver-9.7367987?cmp=rss)

**Vancouver police hand out 1,226 e-scooter tickets: Global BC**
Global News reports that Vancouver police, cracking down on e-scooter riders who were not following the rules, handed out 1,226 tickets since Sept. 4, and that riders overwhelmingly were not wearing helmets. The Vancouver Sun reports VPD saying, "We're not ticketing today. We just want to make sure everyone is safe." Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12086152/vancouver-e-scooter-riders-helmets-police/) , https://vancouversun.com/news/riding-e-scooter-vancouver-police-are-cracking-down

**Five arrested after Langley dealership extortion probe: Vancouver Sun**
The Vancouver Sun reports five people were arrested after a year-long probe into extortion at a Langley car dealership. Global News reports five foreign nationals were charged with extortion-related crimes. As part of Project E-PURSUANCE, police said, four men were arrested in Surrey on Thursday, and one man, a resident of India, was arrested at Toronto Pearson International Airport. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/five-arrested-extortion-langley-car-dealership-rcmp) , https://globalnews.ca/news/12085588/5-foreign-nationals-charged-extortion-related-crimes-bc/

**Trial hears of wrong-way drive before West Vancouver crash: North Shore News**
A trial has heard that a woman drove the wrong way on a West Vancouver highway for more than 2 km before a head-on collision that killed two people. North Shore News reports the crash killed two international students and injured two more. She is accused; the court is hearing the case. Source: [nsnews.com](https://www.nsnews.com/local-news/woman-drove-wrong-way-on-west-vancouver-highway-over-2-km-before-head-on-collision-that-killed-two-trial-hears-12853078)

### City & Province
**PST now applies to textiles, tailoring and cobbling: CBC British Columbia**
Provincial sales tax will now be charged on textile materials, including yarn, natural fibres, synthetic thread, most fabric and clothing patterns, and on tailoring and cobbling services. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/textiles-tailoring-materials-provincial-service-tax-bc-9.7367477?cmp=rss)

**Surrey voters face two elections, one week apart: The Globe and Mail**
The Globe and Mail reports this is the first overlap of municipal and provincial elections since B.C.'s Election Act was passed in 1995. In Surrey, more than 380,000 eligible voters are asked to choose a mayor, eight councillors and six school trustees on Oct. 17, then an MLA on Oct. 24. The city has nearly 100 municipal candidates, and at least 20 provincial candidates are expected across 10 ridings. Premier David Eby called the snap election on Sept. 22, and experts warn turnout could suffer, especially in municipal races planned years earlier. Saanich resident Robert Randall, who ran unsuccessfully for Victoria council in 2008, says the overlap is confusing because affordability, homelessness and housing draw many of the same answers at both levels. The Globe reports two upstart right-wing parties say they will compete in a majority of the 93 ridings. Source: [theglobeandmail.com](https://www.theglobeandmail.com/canada/article-bc-candidates-and-voters-scramble-to-get-their-minds-around-two/)

**Eby campaigns in Nelson on softwood and old growth: My Nelson Now**
My Nelson Now reports B.C. NDP Leader David Eby stopped in Nelson on Friday after campaigning in Kelowna, attended the Nelson Leafs' 7-5 win over the Columbia Valley Rockies in a Leafs hoodie, and visited the locker room. He said he was discussing affordability, U.S. trade measures and support for local industries, and that softwood is hard hit in the region. He named Kalesnikoff and Spearhead as companies affected, and said mass timber and high-end work mean more jobs per tree. Ahead of an old-growth rally on Sunday at Nelson City Hall, he said land-use planning and old-growth restrictions preserve the full ecosystem rather than assessing sites one by one. He said the B.C. Conservatives' plan is to lift those restrictions and clear-cut, which he called the wrong approach, and he praised Kootenay Central candidate Brittny Anderson and Kootenay-Monashee candidate Steve Morissette. Source: [mynelsonnow.com](https://www.mynelsonnow.com/80681/news/elections/2026-bc-election/eby-brings-campaign-tour-to-kootenays/)

**North Vancouver RCMP investigate assaults linked to Grindr: CBC British Columbia**
CBC reports North Vancouver RCMP are investigating a series of assaults. Police say the victims were targeted through the Grindr dating app. A Pride group has issued a safety warning. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/north-vancouver-grindr-assaults-9.7367926?cmp=rss)

### Getting Around
Highway 99 night work in Delta, from Ladner Trunk Road to Highway 17, starts Sunday and runs through Oct. 18, from 9:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m. Monday to Saturday, with one lane open each way. The Dollarton Highway on-ramps are closed Tuesday and Wednesday: eastbound traffic is detoured via Riverside Drive, Mount Seymour Parkway and the Keith Road interchange, and westbound via Main Street, Brooksbank Avenue and the Mountain Highway interchange. On Highway 1, traffic stays shifted north of the median around 256th Street and crosses back near Lefeuvre Road, with the existing eastbound lanes closed around the clock until Oct. 31; in Langley, northbound and southbound traffic on 264 Street is shifted west onto a new bridge until Oct. 17. No watches or warnings are in effect. Saturday clears this morning as fog patches fade, with a northwest wind at 20 km/h, a high of 18 except 22 inland and a UV index of 4; the night low is 10, and Sunday's high is 18 except 23 inland, with a low of 9. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) , https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml

### Sports
**Flames visit the Canucks tonight: Inside The Rink**
The Calgary Flames visit the Vancouver Canucks at Rogers Arena on Saturday, with puck drop at 7:00 p.m. PDT. Inside the Rink lists Calgary at 0-1-0 and Vancouver at 1-1-0 with 2 points. FOX Sports 550 The ZONE says the game is on ESPN+ at 10 p.m. ET. Calgary opened the season with a 6-1 home loss to the Seattle Kraken. Source: [insidetherink.com](https://insidetherink.com/nhl-game-preview-calgary-flames-at-vancouver-canucks-with-line-combinations-10-03-2026/) , https://550thezone.iheart.com/content/2026-10-03-flames-vs-canucks-time-tv-live-stream-1032026/

**Lions visit the Argonauts this afternoon: American Football International**
The B.C. Lions play the Toronto Argonauts at BMO Field on Saturday at 3:00 p.m. ET. Chad Kelly is out with a hand injury, so Nick Arbuckle leads Toronto. The Lions have won seven of their last eight, including a 31-24 win over Saskatchewan; Toronto has won four in a row, most recently 30-28 over Winnipeg, and won the first meeting with the Lions 26-12. The Lions have reached the end zone on 39 of 52 red-zone trips and average 428.5 yards of net offence over 14 games, with Nathan Rourke at quarterback. In Canada the game is on TSN, CTV and Crave. Source: [americanfootballinternational.com](https://www.americanfootballinternational.com/livestream-cfl-bc-lions-toronto-argonauts-octo-3-2100-cet-9-pm-3-pm-et/)

### What's On
**Japan Market Fall Festival at Robson Square: Anywhere Vancouver**
The Japan Market Fall Festival is at the Robson Square Ice Rink, 800 Robson St., on Oct. 3 and 4, from 10 a.m. to 5 p.m., with more than 80 vendors and tickets starting at $4. Source: [anywherevancouver.com](https://anywherevancouver.com/things-to-do-in-metro-vancouver-this-weekend-october-2-4-2026/)

### Both Sides: A cap on staple grocery margins
What is on the table is a campaign promise, not a statute passed this week. At a Kelowna stop on Friday, B.C. NDP Leader David Eby committed to capping profits on some staple products and to steps he said would increase competition. The party billed it as taking the fight to big grocery companies.

Eby's case is that families are paying more while grocery companies' profits rise. He said corporate retailers are using inflation as a cover to raise prices on essential goods, and that "we've all seen our grocery bills go up and up while the profits of grocery giants soar." He singled out Save-On-Foods owner Jimmy Pattison and the Weston family, owners of Loblaws, saying their net worth rose by $4.4 billion in the last year while families struggle. He said not to worry about Save-On-Foods or Jimmy Pattison, who would land on his feet, and that families have to be protected. The price guard, which he compared to a fuel price guard promised the day before, would be a hard ceiling on retail profit margins for milk, cheese, butter and poultry, items that already have wholesale prices managed by marketing boards. The party said that would prohibit unfair markups. He also promised clear per-unit pricing to curb shrinkflation, and a ban on real estate deals and property controls that big chains use to keep smaller stores from opening nearby.

The counterweight in Times Colonist columnist Les Leyne's account is the last grocery promise. Leyne reports the NDP had promised a $1,000 grocery rebate to every family, then abandoned it four months after the election. Asked about that, Eby said his government eliminated the carbon tax, a $2-billion-a-year cut in the tax take. Leyne writes that later price hikes erased a portion of the savings at the pump, after the federal government eliminated the national carbon tax and left B.C. to follow. Both Eby and the column treat rising grocery bills as the problem this promise is aimed at. The commitment was made Friday in Kelowna. Source: [timescolonist.com](https://www.timescolonist.com/opinion/les-leyne-eby-takes-on-grocery-prices-again-12851984)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **A one-million-barrel-a-day oil pipeline to the B.C. coast is now a national-interest project.**

**What You Need to Know:** Ottawa and Alberta have designated a proposed pipeline carrying one million barrels of oil a day from Alberta to the B.C. coast as the first project in the national interest. The Vancouver Sun describes the line as a $44-billion project that Prime Minister Carney tied to jobs, trade beyond the United States, and Canada's energy position. The designation is the decision that landed; it is not a pump-price change for drivers this morning.

### Top Stories
**West Coast oil pipeline becomes 1st project designated in national interest: CBC News**
The federal and Alberta governments have announced that a proposed pipeline carrying one million barrels of oil a day from Alberta to the B.C. coast is the first project designated in the national interest. The Vancouver Sun reports Canada is fast-tracking the $44-billion Alberta-to-B.C. oil pipeline. Prime Minister Carney cited its ability to create jobs, diversify away from the United States as a trade partner, and boost Canada's position as a global energy superpower. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/politics/west-coast-pipeline-national-interest-9.7365037?cmp=rss) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/canada-proposed-44-billion-alberta-bc-oil-pipeline-project-national-interest)

**Deal reached to reopen shuttered Howe Sound pulp mill, union says: CBC News**
A union representing B.C. pulp mill workers says a shuttered facility in Howe Sound is set to reopen later this month. The union says it is welcoming that news. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/howe-sound-pulp-mill-reopen-9.7366417?cmp=rss)

**1 dead, 1 critically injured after train strikes pickup truck in Maple Ridge: CBC News**
Maple Ridge RCMP say a woman is dead and a man was critically injured after a pickup truck was struck by a train on Wednesday. The Vancouver Sun reports police say the train operator is operating, CPKC police were notified, and RCMP collision investigators were called to the scene. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/maple-ridge-bc-train-pickup-collision-9.7365412?cmp=rss) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/truck-struck-train-maple-ridge)

### City & Province
**Former chief coroner Lisa Lapointe to run for B.C. Greens in Saanich South: CBC News**
The B.C. Green Party unveiled former chief coroner Lisa Lapointe on Thursday as a candidate in Saanich South. The announcement is a campaign candidacy in the provincial election, not a policy already in force. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/lisa-lapointe-chief-coroner-bc-greens-election-9.7366183?cmp=rss)

**‘You cannot tax your way to cheaper housing’: CHBA-CO reacts to Eby election pledge: Journal of Commerce**
The Canadian Home Builders' Association, Central Okanagan, responded to an election pledge by Premier David Eby with the line that you cannot tax your way to cheaper housing. The comment is the association's reaction, attributed to CHBA-CO, not a council or legislative vote. Source: [canada.constructconnect.com](https://canada.constructconnect.com/joc/news/associations/2026/10/you-cannot-tax-your-way-to-cheaper-housing-chba-co-reacts-to-eby-election-pledge)

### Getting Around
DriveBC lists two closures that change the next few commutes. Eastbound and westbound Dollarton Highway on-ramps are closed from Sunday, October 4, until Tuesday, October 6, with detours: eastbound via Riverside Drive, Mount Seymour Parkway and the Keith Road interchange, and westbound via Main Street, Brooksbank Avenue and the Mountain Highway interchange. Highway 99 paving in Vancouver runs from Thursday, October 8, until Sunday, October 11, from 11:00 p.m. to 5:00 a.m., Thursday through Saturday, with single-lane alternating traffic; southbound traffic is open to buses and emergency vehicles only, and DriveBC says to expect congestion delays. Environment Canada has no watches or warnings in effect. Current conditions are light rain and 12.9°C. Friday is mainly cloudy, with a 60 percent chance of showers this morning and early this afternoon, a high of 17 and a UV index of 3. Friday night is partly cloudy, with fog patches and a low of 11. Saturday clears in the morning, with fog dissipating, a northwest wind of 20 km/h and a high of 17, except 21 inland. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml)

### Sports
**Oilers, Canucks take lessons from wild games: Global News**
The Edmonton Oilers beat the Vancouver Canucks 9-7 on Thursday night in Vancouver, after the Canucks' 6-5 overtime win in Edmonton on Tuesday. The Oilers are 1-0-1 and the Canucks are 1-1-0. Connor McDavid scored a goal and had four assists, his 15th career five-point game, and said nobody was celebrating because the game has to look different. Leon Draisaitl had two goals and an assist. Evan Bouchard added a goal and two assists and now has eight points in two games, breaking the NHL record for a defenceman in the first two games of a season; Harry Cameron of the 1917-18 Toronto Arenas had seven. Kevin Lankinen was pulled after eight goals on 20 shots, and Leevi Merilainen made 10 saves. Devon Levi stopped 15 of 22 shots. Oilers coach Mike Babcock said the club took three of a possible four points and has to play a full 60 minutes. Canucks coach Manny Malhotra said the game showed how players respond when it gets hard. Brock Boeser said Edmonton was hungrier in the first period. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12085223/oilers-canucks-take-lessons-from-wild-games/) Source: [fieldlevelmedia.com](https://fieldlevelmedia.com/news/evan-bouchard-connor-mcdavid-make-waves-as-oilers-beat-canucks-9-7/) Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/i-watched-this-game-canucks-oilers-16-goals)

### Both Sides: Gas tax cuts and price caps at the pumps
Premier David Eby and the B.C. NDP are offering a gas-tax cut and price caps at the pumps if the party is re-elected. Global News reports Eby said the measures would save the average two-car family up to $100 per month and would cost the provincial treasury about $250 million. My Powell River Now reports the same pledge: a gas-tax cut and price caps if the NDP is re-elected. This is a campaign promise. It is not a tax change already on the books.

The case for the pledge, as Eby makes it, starts with the household fuel bill. He said an average two-car family could save up to $100 a month. The Vancouver Sun reports that small business groups welcome the proposal. Their published reason lines up with his: people and businesses who buy fuel would pay less if the tax cut and the caps took effect. That welcome is the strongest non-government case for the pledge in today's coverage.

The case against, in the same Vancouver Sun report, is that at least one economist said the policy will have little impact. The objection does not deny that pump prices matter. It says this design is unlikely to move the price drivers pay by much. Eby is selling a monthly saving. The economist's reported view is that the saving may not arrive.

What both treatments accept is that the tax cut and the caps are a re-election offer, with a treasury cost Eby put at about $250 million, not a completed change at the station. What happens next is the election. Drivers do not get a new pump price from this pledge today. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12084816/bc-ndp-lower-gas-costs-bc-conservatives-embrace-pipeline/) Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/can-bc-ndp-cap-industry-margins-on-diesel-and-gas) Source: [mypowellrivernow.com](https://www.mypowellrivernow.com/65120/news/elections/2026-bc-election/eby-promises-gas-tax-cut-price-caps-at-the-pumps-if-ndp-is-re-elected/)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **Two pedestrians are dead after being struck near Tsawwassen Mills.**

**What You Need to Know:** Delta police say two pedestrians are dead after being struck near the entrance of Tsawwassen Mills mall, and that the incident is not related to a nearby Truth and Reconciliation Day walk. An Abbotsford transfer-station employee is in hospital with life-threatening injuries after a commercial vehicle struck them, and BC Ferries is headed toward a $1.3-billion fuel contract with a US-owned supplier.

### Top Stories
**Two dead after pedestrians struck near Tsawwassen Mills: Vancouver Sun**
Two pedestrians are dead after being struck near the entrance of Tsawwassen Mills mall. Delta police say the incident is not related to a nearby Truth and Reconciliation Day walk. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/tsawwassen-mills-police-incident-pedestrians-struck)

**Employee struck by vehicle at Abbotsford garbage transfer station: CityNews**
An employee was struck by a commercial vehicle at a garbage transfer station in Abbotsford around 8 a.m. Wednesday at the station on Vye Road and Sumas Way. The Abbotsford Police Department says the employee was taken to hospital with serious, life-threatening injuries. AbbyPD says it is working with WorkSafeBC on an investigation. The transfer station was closed for that investigation. Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/09/30/worker-struck-abbotsford-garbage-transfer/)

**BC Ferries heads toward a $1.3-billion deal with a US-owned fuel supplier: The Tyee**
BC Ferries is headed toward a $1.3-billion deal with a US-owned fuel supplier. The Tyee reports that, despite Premier David Eby’s “buy Canadian” focus, a firm with MAGA connections is the likely contract winner. Source: [thetyee.ca](https://thetyee.ca/News/2026/10/01/BC-Ferries-US-Owned-Fuel-Supplier/)

**Families plan an RCMP complaint against a Vancouver mining firm: CBC British Columbia**
Families of workers at a Canadian mining firm plan to file an RCMP complaint against the Vancouver-based company, their lawyer says. The workers were kidnapped earlier this year in Sinaloa, Mexico, by a suspected cartel commando squad, CBC reports. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/world/vizsla-rcmp-family-9.7363674?cmp=rss)

### City & Province
**Seniors group says long-term care wait times need to be addressed: Vancouver Sun**
A seniors group says long-term care wait times need to be addressed in the B.C. election. B.C. seniors advocate Dan Levitt highlighted in a report earlier this year that the NDP decision to delay construction of seven long-term care facilities was detrimental in a province struggling to keep up with an aging population. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-election-long-term-care-wait-times-need-to-be-addressed-seniors-group-says)

**Vancouver mayoral candidates plan to take on public safety: Global News**
Vancouver mayoral candidates plan to take on public safety. An election plebiscite question asks whether the city should formally request the province to use part of the old St. Paul's Hospital for involuntary care beds. Source: [globalnews.ca](https://globalnews.ca/news/12083414/vancouver-mayoral-candidates-public-safety-plan/)

### Getting Around
Eastbound and westbound Dollarton Highway on-ramps are closed for paving from Sunday, October 4, until Monday, October 5, with detours in effect: eastbound via Riverside Drive, Mount Seymour Parkway and the Keith Road interchange, and westbound via Main Street, Brooksbank Avenue and the Mountain Highway interchange. The Exit 29 River Road ramp in Delta stays closed until Thursday, October 1, from 10:00 p.m. to 1:00 p.m. the next day. On Highway 1, eastbound lanes stay closed around 256th Street until October 31, with traffic shifted north of the median and crossing back near Lefeuvre Road. Highway 91A is down to one lane each way for overnight bridge maintenance until November 15.
No watches or warnings are in effect. Vancouver is mostly cloudy and 11.3°C. Thursday is mainly cloudy, with a 30 percent chance of showers this morning, a high of 15 except 18 inland, and a UV index of 3. Thursday night is cloudy, with a 30 percent chance of showers this evening and a low of 11. Friday is mainly cloudy, with a 60 percent chance of showers in the morning and a high of 17. Source: [drivebc.ca](https://www.drivebc.ca/) Source: [weather.gc.ca](https://weather.gc.ca/rss/weather/49.245_-123.115_e.xml)

### Sports
**Vancouver Whitecaps to remain at BC Place for now: Inside World Football**
The Vancouver Whitecaps are to remain at BC Place for now. Source: [insideworldfootball.com](https://www.insideworldfootball.com/2026/10/01/vancouver-whitecaps-to-remain-at-bc-place-for-now/)

### What's On
**VIFF documentaries highlight Terry Fox and Rick Hansen: CityNews**
Two documentaries at the Vancouver International Film Festival look at British Columbians Terry Fox and Rick Hansen. Run Terry Run, directed by Sean Menard and running 108 minutes, follows Fox’s Marathon of Hope from April 12, 1980, in St. John’s, Newfoundland, aimed at raising $1 million for cancer research, through 143 days of running. It screens at the Vancouver Playhouse on Sunday, October 4, at 1:45 p.m., and at International Village on October 5 at 5:30 p.m. Man in Motion: The Rick Hansen Story, directed by Adrian Buitenhuis and running 96 minutes, follows Hansen’s 1985 journey and the 40,000-kilometre trek he completed. It shows at the Vancouver Playhouse on Saturday. Source: [vancouver.citynews.ca](https://vancouver.citynews.ca/2026/09/30/viff-documentaries-terry-fox-and-rick-hansen/)

### Both Sides: The Vancouver Aquatic Centre pool
CBC British Columbia reports that the Vancouver Aquatic Centre may get a 50-metre pool after all, and it links that possibility to the election. The rebuild had plans to build a 25-metre pool. Parties vying for votes are now promising to build a full-sized competition pool as part of the same Vancouver Aquatic Centre rebuild.

The case for the larger pool, as CBC reports it, is that campaign promise: parties seeking votes say they will build a full-sized competition pool, the pool CBC describes as 50 metres, inside the rebuild. That promise is a promise in a campaign, not a pool already approved in the item CBC published.

The case for the shorter pool is the plan already on the project. CBC reports that the rebuild was set to build a 25-metre pool, and it sets the new promises against that plan. The standing design, on CBC’s account, is the 25-metre tank, and the competition-length pool is what those parties are offering to change it to.

The fact both positions share, in that report, is the rebuild itself: the 25-metre plan and the full-sized promise are about the same Vancouver Aquatic Centre project. What is not yet a decision, on CBC’s wording, is the larger pool: the centre “may” get it, and the parties are “promising” it while they vie for votes. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/vancouver-aquatic-centre-50-metre-pool-9.7362607?cmp=rss)

# Vancouver Daily News
> **A one-point-two-billion-dollar ocean fund arrives before Thursday's West Coast pipeline decision.**

**What You Need to Know:** Prime Minister Mark Carney's $1.2 billion for West Coast ocean protection is in, ahead of an expected Thursday decision on fast-tracking a $44 billion oil pipeline from Alberta to B.C. A B.C. court has dropped drug charges against a Vancouver compassion club and found the federal drug statute unconstitutional on safe supply, with the ruling on hold for six months. Fundraisers hit $3 million for a South Peace MRI, and the Conservation Officer Service is warning of more grizzlies on the Sunshine Coast.

### Top Stories
**$1.2 billion for oceans before an Alberta-B.C. pipeline call: Vancouver Sun**
Prime Minister Mark Carney made a $1.2 billion announcement Tuesday to protect West Coast oceans, the Vancouver Sun reports. A decision is expected Thursday on whether to fast-track a proposed $44 billion oil pipeline from Alberta to B.C. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/business/alberta-bc-oil-pipeline-fast-track-decision-deadline)

**Fundraisers hit $3 million for a Dawson Creek MRI: CBC British Columbia**
The Dawson Creek and District Hospital Foundation says fundraisers have hit a $3 million target for an MRI at the city's new hospital. CBC reports it would be the first publicly funded MRI in B.C.'s South Peace, where patients travel long distances and face long waitlists for diagnostic services. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/dawson-creek-mri-new-hospital-9.7361774?cmp=rss)

**Safety board finds gaps in a Squamish boat crash: CBC British Columbia**
Canada's Transportation Safety Board has found a series of gaps behind a 2024 collision between a tugboat and a workboat at the Woodfibre LNG site near Squamish. CBC reports one of the vessels sank. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/boat-crash-2024-squamish-report-9.7363087?cmp=rss)

**Grizzly sightings up on the Sunshine Coast: Vancouver Sun**
The B.C. Conservation Officer Service is warning of increased grizzly bear sightings on the Sunshine Coast. The Vancouver Sun links a poor berry crop and an increase in the bear population to reports in Pender Harbour, Madeira Park and Sechelt. Source: [vancouversun.com](https://vancouversun.com/news/bc-conservation-officer-service-warns-of-increased-grizzly-bear-sightings-on-sunshine-coast)

### City & Province
**August home sales and prices edged higher: Business in Vancouver**
Bryan Yu writes in Business in Vancouver that B.C. home sales and prices edged higher in August. Wildfires disrupted Interior markets. Source: [biv.com](https://www.biv.com/news/economy-law-politics/bryan-yu-bc-housing-market-recovery-gains-ground-despite-interior-wildfires-rate-pressures-12833121)

**Municipal and provincial votes fall a week apart: CBC British Columbia**
After B.C. NDP Leader David Eby called a snap election, voters are preparing for municipal and provincial elections a week apart, CBC reports. Public administration experts agree that with the campaigns overlapping, voters have a lot to keep track of. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/local-governments-british-columbia-what-is-difference-9.7362643?cmp=rss)

### Both Sides: The drug law and a Vancouver compassion club
A B.C. judge has dropped drug charges against a Vancouver compassion club and ruled the Controlled Drug and Substance Act unconstitutional because it prevents drug users from accessing a safe supply, the Vancouver Sun reports. CBC reports a B.C. Supreme Court judge tossed drug-trafficking convictions against two harm reduction activists who argued they were doing it to reduce the harms caused by toxic drugs.

The Sun's account of the ruling carries that argument to a legal result: the judge found the Act unconstitutional because it blocks drug users from a safe supply.

The strongest case for leaving the statute in place, on the record these reports actually contain, is the court's own pause. The Vancouver Sun says the Supreme Court ruling is put on hold for six months to allow the federal government to change the Controlled Drug and Substance Act. > **Kitimat's multibillion-dollar LNG expansion is going ahead, and it could double coastal exports.**

**What You Need to Know:** LNG Canada says its Phase 2 expansion in Kitimat is moving forward, a project Ottawa is set to call a historic energy investment and one the company says could double exports from that northern plant. A U.S. import ban now blocks some Canadian alcohol, dairy and motorcycles at the border, which lands on B.C. producers. ### Top Stories
**LNG Canada expansion gets go-ahead, as Carney set to highlight 'historic investment' in Canadian energy:** CBC British Columbia
LNG Canada says its multibillion-dollar Phase 2 expansion in Kitimat is going forward. The company says the move could double exports of liquefied natural gas from the northern coastal facility to overseas markets. Prime Minister Carney is set to highlight what is described as a historic investment in Canadian energy. **U.S. bans on Canadian booze hit B.C. producers on one of the trade war's thorniest fronts:** CBC British Columbia
As of Tuesday, some Canadian products, including dairy, motorcycles and alcohol, can no longer cross the border into the United States at all, under an American import ban. CBC British Columbia reports that the ban hits B.C. producers. The outlet describes it as the latest escalation in the Canada-U.S. trade war, and says booze has taken centre stage. **Vancouver transit operator expands into real estate:** The Globe and Mail
TransLink is expanding to become a residential and commercial landlord. In its 2022 investment plan, the agency said it would turn real estate it owns into a revenue source that is not fares and not taxation. The Real Estate Development Program is meant to tighten transit connections and add housing as Metro Vancouver grows. In late July, with PCI Developments, TransLink broke ground on a 31-storey tower at the southwest corner of West Broadway and Arbutus Street in Kitsilano: 256 at-market rental units, 47 below-market rental units, retail space and a public plaza. TransLink chief executive Kevin Quinn and PCI president Tim Grant said the 50/50 partnership came about because the two owned neighbouring properties that would work better as one site. TransLink says it is developing excess land it owns instead of selling it, so it can shape how the buildings are built and how they meet the transit network. The site sits across the street from the future Arbutus Station, the last stop on the Millennium Line extension that is adding six stations along Broadway and linking Burnaby, Port Moody and Coquitlam toward that corridor. PCI's earlier transit hubs include Marine Gateway in Vancouver and the King George Hub in Surrey. ### Both Sides: How West Vancouver luxury homes should be sold
What is being decided, in a market report rather than a council vote, is how homes above $4 million in West Vancouver should be priced and shown this fall. Sotheby's International Realty Canada says the market is firmly in buyers' territory. Its best reason is the count: from Jan. 1 to Aug. 30, 57 properties sold for more than $4 million, a 25 percent decrease from 76 in the same period last year. Managing broker Kevin O'Toole says 195 residential properties were listed above $4 million as of Sept. 1, and that sellers need to be realistic with pricing expectations, conditions and timeframes to attract qualified buyers. The case for a wider net, including a public listing, is also Sotheby's. The firm says its review of land title and MLS records from January 2024 through August 2026 found that one in seven West Vancouver properties above $4 million sells without ever appearing on MLS, and it still says that in current conditions broader public marketing on MLS, with private outreach, is key to attracting qualified purchasers. Chief marketing officer Elaine Hung says that where supply exceeds demand, advisors are encouraging sellers to combine targeted outreach with exposure in premier media and on MLS. Daily Hive, using Zealty, says about 30 homes sold above $4 million in the last 90 days, and that only one of those was ultra-luxury, at $10 million or more. Both readings accept the same drop in sales and the same surplus of listings. The report puts the market in buyers' territory this fall and does not set a date when that would flip. Premier David Eby, asked Wednesday about election timing by CBC Early Edition host Stephen Quinn, said concurrent votes "will give an opportunity for local government leaders to pick a side here as well," Les Leyne reports in the Times Colonist. A provincial election day is set for October 24; Tom Fletcher reports Eby called it on September 22 outside Government House in Victoria.

Eby's case, in that Quinn interview, is that local leaders now face the same choice he wants provincial voters to face. He asked whether they are "on the side for their communities, building out the infrastructure" and "doing that work with the federal government," or "advocates and supporters of the Conservative approach of doubling down on the old way, when we were too closely tied to the U.S., fighting unnecessary culture wars, dividing people and cutting quality programs." Leyne reports various mayors were offended by Tuesday's call, particularly because Eby had been asked at the convention to wait his turn. He appeared there, said he would consider it, said he understood their anxiety, and said no decision had been made. Four days later, he called the election.

> **Premier David Eby has called a snap provincial election for October 24, citing an existential U.S. trade threat.**

**What You Need to Know:** Premier David Eby called a snap B.C. election for October 24, framing it around U.S. trade tensions. The District of Squamish rejected a proposed 10-year, $142-million tax deal with Woodfibre LNG. A Vancouver investment firm will acquire eight Accent Inns and Hotel Zed properties across the province by the end of November.

### What This Show Covers
This is a short morning brief for people who live in Metro Vancouver. It covers what council and the province decided, what those decisions mean for getting around today, how the local teams did, what is on, and one contested local issue presented with the strongest case on each side. The brief is read by Mira, the network's AI host. Stories are chosen and written by software from named local newsrooms and public data sources such as DriveBC and Environment Canada, and every item names its source. The one thing it will not do is speculate about people—no guesses about anyone's motives, guilt, health or private life, and no endorsements at election time. Vancouver Daily News is part of the Nerra Network, an independent, ad-free network of shows at nerranetwork.com. Listeners are invited to visit the site for the full schedule.

### Top Stories
**Eby calls early provincial election on Oct. 24:** My Cariboo Now. Premier David Eby called a snap provincial election for October 24. He cited an existential threat from U.S. trade tensions as the reason for the early vote. Opposition parties have begun reorganizing ahead of the date. British Columbia's political scene is undergoing rapid restructuring as parties adjust to the October 24 date. NDP Leader David Eby framed the vote as necessary to respond to the threat posed by U.S. trade policy. The Conservative Party of B.C. has seen substantial turnover with over a dozen MLAs quitting or being expelled from caucus since August amid internal disputes. Today Peter Milobar and six other MLAs from the breakaway CentreBC party rejoined the Conservatives while Elenore Sturko remained with CentreBC and became its leader. Brent Chapman left the Conservatives to join OneBC. Kerry-Lynne Findlay resigned as leader less than four months after taking the role and Cariboo-Chilcotin MLA Lorne Doerkson took over as interim leader. Source: [mycariboonow.com](https://www.mycariboonow.com/316414/news/politics/eby-calls-early-provincial-election-on-oct-24/)

**District of Squamish rejects $142M Woodfibre LNG deal:** CBC British Columbia. The District of Squamish council turned down a negotiated 10-year tax settlement that would have delivered $142 million from Woodfibre LNG to the Sea-to-Sky community. The decision ends the proposed agreement. The settlement would have seen Woodfibre LNG contribute the funds over the decade in exchange for tax certainty. Council voted against the package after negotiations concluded. Source: [cbc.ca](https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/british-columbia/142m-woodfibre-lng-tax-deal-denied-by-district-of-squamish-council-9.7354771?cmp=rss)

**Vancouver company to acquire all eight Accent Inns and Hotel Zed hotels:** Daily Hive Vancouver. Synvest Group of Companies will buy the eight Accent Inns and Hotel Zed properties across British Columbia with the transfer expected at the end of November. The hotels total roughly 800 rooms. All existing bookings will be honoured and operations continue normally. The acquisition covers five Accent Inns properties in Richmond, Burnaby, Victoria, Kelowna and Kamloops plus Hotel Zed locations in Victoria, Kelowna and Tofino along with the ROAR restaurant at Hotel Zed Tofino. The largest property is Accent Inns Vancouver Airport in Richmond with over 200 rooms. Mandy Farmer CEO of the selling company said the day was emotional and that it mattered to find a new owner who understood the company culture. Azim Virani founder and principal of Synvest said the family has always viewed hospitality as being about people and that Synvest wants to work with existing teams to preserve the established approach. Source: [dailyhive.com](https://dailyhive.com/vancouver/accent-inns-hotel-zed-synvest-acquisition)

**VPD Seizes Record 328.55 kg Cocaine Worth $5.8M in Shipping Container:** VancouverPD. Vancouver police seized 328.55 kilograms of cocaine valued at an estimated $5.8 million from a shipping container in southeast Vancouver the largest such seizure in the city. Police were called to a Vancouver-based company on July 21 after staff located 14 duffle bags of drugs hidden amongst boxes of t-shirts that formed a legitimate order. Sergeant Travis Fraser of the VPD Drug Unit said the business was shocked and called police right away and is in no way associated with the seized cocaine. The amount of drugs as well as the stamps and packaging clearly indicates organized crime is behind the shipment he said. The investigation showed the shipping container originated in Honduras on May 18 2026 was loaded onto a vessel stopped in Jamaica on June 6 2026 and arrived in Montreal on July 5 2026. Fraser said police believe the cocaine was supposed to be removed prior to its arrival at the company. VPD continues to liaise with law enforcement and port authority counterparts in Canada Honduras Jamaica the United States Drug Enforcement Agency and the RCMP. ### Both Sides: Woodfibre LNG tax settlement
Supporters of the deal argued it would provide stable long-term revenue for local services and infrastructure without raising resident taxes allowing the district to plan capital projects with certainty. They noted the funds would arrive over a decade giving the municipality predictable income that could support roads parks and emergency services in the Sea-to-Sky region. Opponents maintained that the project carries unacceptable environmental and safety risks to the Sea-to-Sky corridor and that accepting the funds would lock the community into supporting expanded LNG operations for a decade. They pointed to potential impacts on air quality marine traffic and emergency response capacity along the narrow corridor between Squamish and Whistler.
